title: Interpreting formula
competency: Interpret formulas qualitatively and quantitatively, using coefficients and subscripts.

keywords.def: The number in front of a symbol or formula. In 3H₂O it is 3.
The small number after a symbol. In H₂O the 2 is a subscript.

en.text: A formula has a qualitative meaning, which elements, and a quantitative meaning, how many. The coefficient in front counts atoms or molecules: 3H₂O is three water molecules. The subscript after a symbol counts atoms in one molecule: Cl₂ has two chlorine atoms.

screens.title: The big number in front
screens.after: The 3 in front is the coefficient. It counts the molecules: 3 water molecules.

screens.title: 3.2.7 Interpreting formula
paras: A formula gives qualitative and quantitative meanings.
Qualitative: which kind of element or elements.
Quantitative: how many atoms or molecules.

screens.title: Qualitative meaning
paras: The symbol O stands for an atom of oxygen. Fe stands for iron metal.
CaO stands for calcium oxide, from calcium and oxygen.
Ca(NO₃)₂ stands for calcium nitrate: one calcium and two nitrate groups.

screens.title: Quantitative meaning
paras: The number before a symbol is the coefficient. 2Fe is two atoms of iron.
A subscript after a symbol shows a molecule. Cl₂ is a chlorine molecule of two atoms.
A coefficient before a formula counts molecules. 2CO₂ is two molecules of carbon dioxide.
4NaCl is four formula units of sodium chloride.

screens.title: Coefficient or subscript?
screens.ask: Tap each one to see what its numbers mean.
items: Subscript 2: one chlorine molecule of two atoms.
Coefficient 2: two molecules. Each has 1 C and 2 O.
Coefficient 4: four formula units of sodium chloride.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The number in front of a symbol or formula. In 3H₂O it is 3.
The small number after a symbol. In H₂O the 2 is a subscript.

screens.text: Read the formula 4O₃: what are the coefficient and the subscript?
screens.why:
The coefficient is the big number in front: 4.
The subscript is the small number after O: 3.
So 4O₃ is 4 ozone molecules, each with 3 O atoms.
Answer: 4 and 3.

The coefficient 3 counts molecules.
H₂O is a water molecule, not an atom.
So 3H₂O is 3 water molecules.
"6 H molecules" is wrong: the H atoms are inside the water molecules.
screens.clue: H₂O is a molecule, not an atom.

screens.text: True or false: O₂ and 2O have the same meaning.
screens.why:
In O₂ the 2 is a subscript: one molecule of two joined atoms.
In 2O the 2 is a coefficient: two separate atoms.
Same number of atoms, but a different meaning.
The statement is false.
screens.clue: Is the 2 a coefficient or a subscript?

screens.title: Counting atoms in 4H₂O
steps: So 4H₂O has 8 hydrogen atoms and 4 oxygen atoms.

screens.ask: Count the atoms: 3H₂ has ___ hydrogen atoms in total.
screens.why:
3H₂ is 3 hydrogen molecules.
Each molecule has 2 atoms.
3 × 2 = 6.
Answer: 6.
screens.clue: Multiply the coefficient by the subscript.

screens.title: Atoms or molecules?
screens.text: Sort each one: separate atoms, one molecule, or several molecules?
items: Coefficient 2, no subscript: two O atoms.
Subscript 2: one molecule of two atoms.
One nitrogen molecule of two atoms.
screens.why:
A coefficient with no subscript counts separate atoms: 2O, 3Fe.
A subscript alone shows one molecule: O₂, N₂.
A coefficient before a molecule counts molecules: 2H₂O, 3CO₂.
screens.clue: Is there a number in front, a small number after, or both?

screens.ask: Count the atoms: 2Ca(NO₃)₂ has ___ oxygen atoms in total.
screens.why:
One NO₃ group has 3 O.
(NO₃)₂ has 2 groups: 2 × 3 = 6 O.
The 2 in front means 2 formula units.
2 × 6 = 12.
Answer: 12.
screens.clue: The 2 after the bracket multiplies NO₃; the 2 in front multiplies everything.

items.why:
The coefficient 3 counts molecules.
H₂O is a water molecule, not an atom.
So 3H₂O is 3 water molecules.
"6 H molecules" is wrong: the H atoms are inside the water molecules.

items.text: What is the qualitative meaning of 2Fe?
items.why:
Qualitative means which kind of element.
Fe is the symbol of iron.
The 2 tells how many: that is the quantitative meaning.
Answer: iron (the element).

items.text: What is the qualitative meaning of CO₂?
opts: Carbon dioxide, from carbon and oxygen
items.ans: Carbon dioxide, from carbon and oxygen
items.why:
Qualitative means which kinds of element.
C is carbon; O is oxygen.
So CO₂ is carbon dioxide, made from carbon and oxygen.

items.text: What is the qualitative meaning of O₂?
items.why:
O tells the element: oxygen.
The subscript 2 shows two joined atoms.
So O₂ stands for an oxygen molecule.
Two separate atoms would be written 2O.

items.text: What is the quantitative meaning of 3H₂?
items.why:
The coefficient 3 counts molecules: 3 molecules.
Each molecule has 2 H atoms.
3 × 2 = 6 H atoms.
Answer: 3 molecules, 6 H atoms.

items.text: What is the quantitative meaning of 4H₂O?
items.why:
The coefficient 4 counts molecules: 4 water molecules.
H: 4 × 2 = 8 atoms.
O: 4 × 1 = 4 atoms.
Answer: 4 molecules, 8 H and 4 O.

items.text: What is the quantitative meaning of 2NaCl?
items.why:
The coefficient 2 counts formula units.
Na: 2 × 1 = 2. Cl: 2 × 1 = 2.
Answer: 2 formula units, 2 Na and 2 Cl.

test.text: In 2CO₂, what is the 2 in front called?
test.why:
A number in front of a formula is the coefficient.
It counts molecules: 2 molecules of CO₂.
The small 2 after O is the subscript.
Answer: coefficient.

test.text: What does the formula Cl₂ mean?
opts: one chlorine molecule of two atoms
test.ans: one chlorine molecule of two atoms
test.why:
The 2 is a subscript after Cl.
A subscript shows atoms joined in one molecule.
So Cl₂ is one chlorine molecule of two atoms.
Two separate atoms would be 2Cl.

test.ask: Count the atoms: 2H₂O has ___ hydrogen atoms.
test.why:
2H₂O is 2 water molecules.
Each has 2 H atoms.
2 × 2 = 4.
Answer: 4.

test.text: True or false: 2Fe stands for two atoms of iron.
test.why:
Fe is iron, written as a single atom.
The coefficient 2 counts the atoms.
So 2Fe is two iron atoms.
The statement is true.

test.ask: Count the atoms: 3CaCO₃ has ___ oxygen atoms.
test.why:
One CaCO₃ has 3 O atoms.
The coefficient 3 means 3 formula units.
3 × 3 = 9.
Answer: 9.
